newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish prosecutor sees no need to call Gonzalez.
newsitem.headline: Spanish prosecutor sees no need to call Gonzalez.

text.p: Spain's state prosecutor told the Supreme Court on Monday he saw no grounds to question former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez about a 1980s "dirty war" against Basque separatist rebels, state radio said.

The state prosecution, which had already advised against calling the Socialist leader earlier this year, said there was no reason to change that opinion despite fresh charges that Gonzalez knew of an illegal campaign that killed 28 people.
The state prosecutor was addressing the Supreme Court in a session at which the tribunal must decide whether it wants to question Gonzalez as a witness, as a suspect, or not at all.
The prosecution's opinion is important but is not binding for the court.

Gonzalez, who lost elections in March after 13 years in power, denies chares by former security chiefs and disgruntled fellow Socialists that he knew of the 1983-87 campaign of bombings, kidnappings, torture and murders by members of the security forces and hired gunmen.

The second chamber of the Supreme Court, which deals with cases involving members of parliament like Gonzalez, was expected to make up its mind on whether to question the ex-premier before 3 p.m. (1400 GMT).
